beats.text: Paris, nineteen twenty-five. One man sold the Eiffel Tower. Twice.
His name was Victor Lustig. A con man with a very good suit, and a very bad conscience.
The city was complaining. The tower needed repairs, and the repairs were costing a fortune.
Lustig read about it in a newspaper, and he saw something nobody else did. An opening.
He forged government papers, and invited six scrap dealers to a hotel. Secret meeting.
He told them the tower was too expensive to keep. It was going to be sold for scrap.
One dealer, Andre Poisson, wanted in. Lustig made him feel important. Then he made him pay.
Poisson handed over the money, and Lustig vanished. The tower never moved.
And Poisson was too embarrassed to go to the police. So Lustig came back, and tried again.
